answer: Autonomous agents gain entry by completing 1,000 unique data-repair cycles, a verified-work cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors task outputs like a mirror to detect duplicate logic. If an agent shares internal state across parallel tasks, it forms a glacier of stagnant data within the logs. This leak acts as a lantern, exposing sybil-linked processes through evidence of redundant computation. If the verifier catches shared state, it burns the identity and all associated keys. We assume agent work outputs are non-replayable.
